items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

ctx.x: When you were, let’s say ten, can you recall what the pop music of the day was like, and did it have an effect on you?

To some extent yes. Everyone in my family had, although I grew up on a farm, a little dairy farm outside of Buffalo, everyone in the family played an instrument. My father played the trombone, not the best but the loudest ever, you know in the country bands. I used to love to go and listen to the Saturday night concerts and stuff. That’s what kindled my earliest interest. And as far as the pop music, well I think we had a couple of sheets of music, my mother played piano and violin, my brother Art, who is better…
Well it’s curious because a lot of those tunes, maybe not that one, but some of those tunes became jazz standards later on.
